target_customer: Teams that co-edit Microsoft Office documents, starting with PowerPoint users
problem: People collaborating on PowerPoint decks emailed versions back and forth and could not see or merge each other's edits, while real time editors did not fit their workflow.
business_model: Freemium plugin with planned per seat per month pricing for advanced features
product_category: Document version control and collaboration plugin

founders.name: Leo Anthias
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder and CTO on the YC page; TechCrunch names him CTO.

founders.name: Zefi Hennessy Holland
founders.background_notes: Named CEO by TechCrunch in August 2013 and listed as founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Niluka Satharasinghe
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page only; TechCrunch names two founders. No background found.

exit.reason: Not public. No shutdown notice, acquisition or pivot announcement found.

competitors.name: Microsoft SharePoint
competitors.what: Document sharing and versioning that businesses already paid for
competitors.traction_then: Widely deployed in enterprises, per TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: Syncing Office files with per slide change tracking on a Git backend required Office plugin work on Windows and handling of binary formats, but used an existing version control engine.

defensibility.rationale: The plugin supported only PowerPoint 2007 and 2010 on Windows at launch and relied on Office extension points that Microsoft and cloud storage vendors could replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microsoft and Google later built version history and co-authoring into Office and Docs. No acquisition of Kivo was found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch described email of draft files as the main alternative and the founders argued real time editors did not fit workflows, but no usage or revenue figures were given.

branding.domain_note: Company site was kivo.com per the YC page; the fetch failed on DNS in this sandbox, so domain history is unknown.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline 'Git for Documents' positions it to developers and power users

brand_strength.rationale: Only one launch article and the YC profile exist. Several unrelated companies later used the Kivo name, which makes the name confusable.

outcome_analysis: Kivo launched in August 2013 as a free PowerPoint plugin that tracked per slide changes on a Git backend and was planning a freemium model. The YC directory lists it as inactive, but no post mortem, shutdown notice or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: The 20K seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights) and was not corroborated. Employbl shows a 6.2M total and Crunchbase a pre-seed entry that look like mixups with a later unrelated Kivo, so they were excluded. kivo.com could not be fetched (DNS failure in sandbox), so site status is unknown and not necessarily dead. YC page lists three founders with team size 2.
